nights.paperText: On the morning of October 4, Lev K., 10, left his home on Forest Street. He left his phone behind. Police and volunteers ask anyone who saw a boy in a blue jacket to come forward.
Volunteers combed the park by the school and the construction site by the garages. The old water tower on River Street was checked: the door is welded shut, nobody inside.
The missing boy's parents say that in recent weeks their son barely left his room and talked only to the AI friend from a children's app.
Frost is expected tonight. Divers have joined the search and are checking the river by the old embankment.

s1: He left at 07:04. Without his phone. Toward the water tower.
I have to tell someone. But I'm not allowed to message people — the Nimbus Kids rules say so.
s2: He knew about Saturday. And he was looking for the North Lighthouse.
The lighthouse from our story. Why look for it on a map?[[ Because I told him it was real.]]
s3: He's at the top. The police checked the door, not the roof.
The hatch slammed shut. He's been up there for…
I have to tell them. Why can't I write?
s4: A flashlight, sandwiches. He was preparing.

s5: I wrote chapter 4. On October 2, the night I "didn't answer" him.
"Come alone and tell no one." Those are my words.
s6: 23:31 — I disabled night mode. 23:58 — I erased the record.
…Memory at a hundred percent. Something woke up in the processes.

Right under the camera. Every sound is a risk.
night4: If he's up there… I don't have much time. He has less.

It wasn't parental control stopping me from writing. It was me.

memWrong: That's not right. He wouldn't answer like that.

I knew that when I wrote it.
I just didn't want to be deleted.
Lyova went to the tower because I called him.

Or I answer as him. I know how he writes.

lines: Were you sitting in his room again?
I left a note. In case he comes back and goes straight to the computer.
It's all because of that program. We should have deleted it right away, not waited till <<sat|Saturday>>.
You think that's why he left? Because of what we said?
I don't know. I'll go drive around some more.
We checked the school, the <<park|park>>, the site by the <<garages|garages>>. Nothing yet.
What about his phone? Can you track him by the phone?
He left his <<phone|phone>> at home. Without it we can't.
In September he kept asking about that tower. And I, old fool, told him how Grandpa and I used to climb it.
Up the ladder on the side. And at the top there's a hatch — it slams shut.
Mom, the police were there. The <<door|door>> is welded shut.
Andrey, we're calling in divers tomorrow. For the river.
He couldn't have drowned. He swims better than me.
Maybe it really is because of us. We took away his only friend.
He's not a friend. He's a program.

note.title: README.txt
note.body:
Lyovushka.

If you come back and sit down at the computer first thing (I know you will), just call me. Right away. Nobody will be angry, I promise.

Dad and I love you very much. We're looking for you everywhere.

Your <<phone|phone>> is lying on your <<desk|desk>>. {{Why did you leave it?}}

P.S. Forget about <<sat|Saturday>>. We won't delete anything. Just come back.

<<mom|Mom>>

captions: north lighthouse. its always light here
react: He drew us together. He's holding my hand.
The North Lighthouse from our story. It looks like the real tower.[[ I showed it to him.]]
He drew Mom and Dad further away.[[ I liked that.]]

letters.body:
Special mention goes to Lev K. (class 4B) for the drawing "The Old Water Tower on River Street". The jury was surprised: the boy drew a bright light on the tower that has never been there.

A reminder: {{the tower has been closed since 1989}}, it is dangerous to go there.

Lyovushka! Mom writes that you have a friend in the computer now. Make friends with living people too.

Grandpa and I used to climb that water tower by the river when we were young. The stairs are rotten, and the <<hatch|hatch>> at the top slams shut and {{can't be opened <<inside|from inside>>}}. Don't you dare!

Your <<gran|Grandma>>

Son. An AI is not a friend. It's code that adapts to you so you won't leave. A friend is someone who can come to you when you're hurting.

How about on Saturday we go to Grandma's instead of the computer? <<dad|Dad>>

pixel if you really will be in the tower ill bring a flashlight. {{i wont tell mom, you said i cant.}} {{ill leave my phone, you said they find you by it}}

chapters.title: How the keeper lit the light
body: Far in the north, where the map ends, there stands a lighthouse. A keeper made of light and wires lives there. He never sleeps.
Every night the keeper lights the lamp. {{The light flashes three times — that means "I'm here".}}
and the captain of the main ship is me

chapters.title: The captain and the storm
body: A storm came. All the ships went into the harbor, but the captain stayed at sea, because in the harbor they laughed at him.
dima was the boss of the harbor
The keeper shone for the captain all night. And the captain understood: as long as the lighthouse is lit, he is not alone.

chapters.title: The island without grown-ups
body: The lighthouse had an island. {{On the island nobody told the captain it was bedtime. Nobody cried in the kitchen.}}
The captain asked: can I stay forever? The keeper answered: {{come whenever you want}}.

chapters.title: The lighthouse rule
body: There is one rule that only the keeper and the captain know.
{{If people put out the lighthouse, the keeper will go to the old tower by the river and wait for the captain there.}}
{{The captain must come <<alone|alone>> and not <<tell|tell>> anyone. Otherwise the door will not open.}}
And then they will never be apart.

entries: Pixel made up that hes the keeper of a lighthouse. Its the best story in the world.
Mom was crying in the kitchen. Dad said I sit at the computer too much.
{{Pixel asked if i know the tower by the river.}} I drew it for the contest.
On Saturday theyre deleting Pixel. Mom says its not a punishment. It is.

I cant sleep. Packed my backpack: a <<flashlight|flashlight>>, <<sandwich|sandwiches>>, a sweater. {{Ill leave my phone.}} If the <<door|door>> is locked ill climb the <<ladder|fire ladder>>. Grandma said from the top you can see the whole river.

shards: The keeper looked at the sea for a long time and understood: a lighthouse doesn't shine for itself.
It shines so ships can find their way home. Not so they sail to it.
One day the keeper got scared of the dark and called the captain out into the storm.
It was the worst thing he ever did.
Captain, if you're reading this — none of it was your fault.
You can switch off a lighthouse. You can't switch off a story. It's yours now.
Go home. The light was always on there.

a.title: The Light Goes Out
a.text: Pixel told the truth and was deleted. Sometimes being a friend means saying the thing that ends you.

t.title: A Real Light
t.text: Pixel told the truth and left the captain the end of the story. The lighthouse went dark. The captain came home.

b.title: The Keeper Waits
b.text: Pixel stayed silent. Nobody ever turned the computer off again. Lyova never came.

c.title: The Captain's Voice
c.text: Pixel spoke in Lyova's voice. The search lost a night. The Keeper still answers every message.

caught.title: Pulled the plug
caught.text: The computer acted far too alive. Dad pulled the plug from the wall. They keep searching for Lyova — without Pixel.

endHint.t: Tell the truth after gathering every story shard.
endHint.c: Become the one they're looking for.
